sentences.text: Shri Santosh Kumar Meena learned counsel for the appell  Shri H.S. Rathore learned counsel for the respondent/st Heard on I.A. No.9637/2025, which is repeat (second) application under Section 430 of the Bharitya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of sole appellant Anil Solanki.
First application of the appellant (I.A. No.2497/2024) was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 12.03.2025.

The present appellant has been convicted for commission of offences punishable under Section 363,
366(A), 376(2), 376(2)(N) of the Indian Penal Code & Section 5(L)/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act and sentenced to undergo 7, 10, 10, 10, 20 years' rigorous imprisonment along with fine of Rs.1000/- for each sections respectively with default stipulations.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: As per the prosecution case, on 23.03.2019 prosecutrix lodged a report at police station Sendhwa Gramin, she is 15 year old girl she resides in village Balkhad.
She is doing housework.
On 27.03.2019, she went to the village of her maternal uncle at Holi festival.

During dancing at about 12:00 am two persons came with motorcycle and they caught hold of the prosecutrix and went to Maharashtra by motorcycle and she lived with 2 CRA-292-2024 appellant for two days in the huts.
In this period appellant has committed rape with the prosecutrix.
On 25.03.2019 prosecutrix has been recovered from the possession of the present appellant.
Counsel for the appellant argued that the prosecution has failed to prove the source of age of the prosecutrix.
It is also argued that the prosecutrix herself had gone on the bike alongwith the appellant and another person.
Counsel for the State opposed the application and submitted that as per the prosecution, the prosecutrix was 16 years, 11 months at the time of incident.

sentences.text: After hearing learned counsel for the parties and considering the facts in entirety and also the statement of the prosecutrix, we find that she was the consenting party as she travelled along with the appellant, where she stayed with him for about two days.
The prosecution did not file any birth certificate, though the case was based on the birth certificate.
Upon going through the statement of prosecutrix, we find that the prosecution has not placed any birth certificate on record.
The age is found to be proved by the trial Court on the basis of the scholar register, where the source for recording the age of the prosecutrix has not been proved.
Apart from that, the appellant was 21 years of age at the time of the incident; the prosecutrix herself had gone on the bike alongwith the appellant and another person.
This is an appeal of 2024, and final hearing of the same will take time.

In the case of Tejubai v/s The State of Madhya Pradesh reported in 2025 (1) MPLJ (Crl.) 75, it has been held that if the date of birth of the prosecutrix in the school 3 CRA-292-2024 register is recorded on the basis of a person who made entry of the date of birth, the same is not sufficient to prove the age.

entities.text: Tejubai v/s The State of Madhya Pradesh reported in 2025 (1) MPLJ (Crl.) 75
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the same, we deem it appropriate to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the present appellant.
Accordingly, I.A. No.9637/2025 stands allowed.

The execution of remaining jail sentence of appellant - Anil Solanki shall remain suspended during the pendency of the appeal and he be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court and on depositing the fine amount (if not already deposited) with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 10.08.2026 , and thereafter, on all subsequent dates as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard during the pendency of the appeal.
Certified copy, as per Rules.
